properties.summary: Incident Type: MOBILE - NRC Report ID: 1060803 - Medium Affected: WATER - Suspected Responsible Party:
properties.content:
Report Details
NRC Report ID: 1060803
Incident Time: 2013-09-20 15:30:00
Nearest City: Denver, CO
Location: LOCATED ON THE WEST SIDE OF THE WEWATTA BLOCK BETWEEN 19TH AND 20TH STREET 1917 CHESTNUT PLACE
Incident Type: MOBILE
Material: OIL, MISC: MOTOR
Medium Affected: WATER
Suspected Responsible Party:
SkyTruth Analysis
Lat/Long: 39.757843, -104.999479 (Approximated from street_address)
Reported Spill Volume: 9 gallon
Report Description
***WEB REPORT***NEAR OUR CONSTRUCTION SITE, WE FOUND EVIDENCE OF AN OIL SPILL OF 8-10 GALLONS ON THE ROAD. THE SPILL LOOKS LIKE IT MAY HAVE BEEN FROM A VEHICLE THAT WAS IN SOME SORT OF WRECK. THERE WERE REMINANTS OF AN OIL PLUG, A FEW BROKEN METAL PIECES, AND A FEW PLASTIC PIECES. SOMEONE HAD PLACED SOME FLOOR DRY MATERIAL ON A SMALL PORTION OF THE SPILL. THE SPILL OCCURRED ON WEWATTA STREET BETWEEN 19TH AND 20TH STREET. THE VEHICLE WAS PARKED IN FRONT OF A STORM SEWER INLET THAT DRAINS TO THE SOUTH PLATTE RIVER. THE INLET HAD A ROCK SOCK IN FRONT OF IT AT THE TIME OF THE SPILL. IT ALSO HAS A FLOGUARD PERMANENT INLET FILTER INSTALLED. THERE WAS STILL ROUGHLY 1-2 GALLONS THAT ENTERED THE CATCH BASIN AND TRAILED INTO THE DRAIN. WE DO NOT KNOW WHO WAS RESPONSIBLE FOR THE SPILL, BUT CLEANED UP AROUND THE INLET AS BEST WE COULD AND REPLACED THE ROCK SOCK.

Report Description***CNUE/NEEC REPORT** INCIDENT NAME: CITIZEN COMPLAINT | OFF SITE SALT IMPACTS | TOMLINSON ENVIRONMENTAL SERVICES LTD. | ST. LAWRENCE RIVER | SOUTH DUNDA, ON INCIDENT CATEGORY: TRANSPORTATION AND WAREHOUSING OVERALL COMPLAINT REGARDING ONGOING SALT SPRAY FROM TOMLINSON"S SALT PAD OPERATIONS SINCE JULY 23, 2025. SALT ACCUMULATION ON VEHICLES, WINDOWS, DOORS, AND DRIVEWAY AT 11579 LAKESHORE DRIVE. VEHICLES FEEL ROUGH TO THE TOUCH DUE TO BAKED-ON SALT. SALT PILES REMAIN UNCOVERED DESPITE EXPECTATIONS THEY BE COVERED WITHIN 24–48 HOURS. CONCERNS ABOUT ENVIRONMENTAL IMPACT ON THE RIVER AND RESIDENTIAL NEIGHBORHOOD. PHOTO EVIDENCE SUBMITTED BY CELL MESSAGE - VIEW ATTACHED. EMAIL: I AM WRITING TODAY TO ADVISE AND DOCUMENT THAT SINCE THE BEGINNING OF THE SALT OPERATIONS FOR 2025 ON JULY 23RD ON THE TOMLINSON SALT PAD, WE HAVE HAD CONTINUAL AMOUNTS OF SALT SPRAY ON OUR VEHICLES AND ALL OF OUR PROPERTY - WINDOWS , DOORS , DRIVEWAY ETC. I HAVE PICTURES OF THE ACCUMULATION ON THE VEHICLES WHICH SHOW THE CONSIDERABLE AMOUNT OF ACCUMULATION. WE CAN FEEL THE SALT RESIDUE ON THE VEHICLES AS IT IS ROUGH TO TOUCH AND THE SUN HAS ACTUALLY BAKED IT ON. MY CAR WAS WASHED SUNDAY MORNING AND NOW THE SALT SPRAY HAS HIT AGAIN. THE SALT PILES HAVE NOT BEEN COVERED AT ALL AFTER OVER A WEEK PLUS TIME. I BELIEVE THEY ARE TO BE COVER WITHIN A 24 TO 48 HOUR TIME FRAME. TODAY THERE IS AN EAST WIND THAT IS FAIRLY BRISK SO I WILL EXPECT WE WILL ONCE AGAIN HAVE CONSIDERABLE AMOUNTS OF SALT RESIDUE. IN ADDITION I AM CERTAIN THAT THE RIVER AND OUR NEIGHBORHOOD IS ALSO BEING AFFECTED WITH THE SALT. THIS IS OUR PROPERTY AND OUR HOME. WE SHOULD NOT BE HAVING TO CLEAN THE SALT SPRAY FROM OUR VEHICLES . WINDOWS AND HOUSE PROPERTY CONTINUALLY. WE DESERVE SOME "RESPECT AND CONSIDERATION". WE SHOULD NOT BE DISREGARDED AS NUISANCE AND DISMISSED. IT IS SUMMER AND WE WOULD LOVE TO BE ABLE TO ENJOY OUR PROPERTY WITHOUT HAVING TO DEAL WITH ALL DAY INTO EVENING NOISE AND SALT SPRAY!

THIS ANOMALY IS BELIEVED TO BE ASSOCIATED WITH EIGHT NOAA NESDIS RESPONSE LINK NRC REPORTS SINCE 7/30/26, MOST RECENTLY #1471670 ON 8/24/26.
